# Holders of BTC::stETH, from the rebalance dilution exploit of 2026-10-16 to the pause

Generated by `script/verify/incidents/RebalanceDilutionReport.t.sol`; run `script/verify/incidents/run-rebalance-dilution-report` to regenerate. Do not edit by hand. The explanation is in [README.md](README.md).

Every party is read on a fork: just before the exploit's transaction `0xb8701591c0fa3ee44a9f42379d167261f70e0532f7c0cea6fcda26ef999df3db` (block 26204584, 2026-10-16 10:45:47 UTC), just after it, at the end of every later block in which the market's minter, pools, manager, pegged or leveraged token or genesis contract logged anything, and at the end of block 26248723, the last before the minters and the pools were paused in block 26248724 (2026-10-22 14:22:23 UTC). What each party did in between comes from those logs, captured from Etherscan in [logs-26204584-26248724/](logs-26204584-26248724/) and, for the genesis contract, [logs-24049000-26248724/](logs-24049000-26248724/).

The parties are every account in the holder capture at the pause, [holders-26248724/](holders-26248724/), with the fee receivers, the reserve pool and the accounts the exploit paid. A party absent from the capture at the exploit's block, [holders-26204584/](holders-26204584/), is new since the exploit. The genesis contract holds the tokens of the genesis participants who have not claimed them: each such participant is a party with its own claim, and the genesis contract's own holdings are those claims together.

Every amount and price is printed in full, to all 18 decimals; only the collateral ratio is rounded. Values are in wstETH, each at its own reading's prices, as in the figures file: an amount of a token times the minter's price for it, over the oracle's price for wstETH, floored to the wei. A party's holdings count the pegged and leveraged tokens in its wallet, its deposits and rewards in both pools and its genesis claim. They leave out the wstETH in its wallet, which also moves for reasons outside the market. The exploit's change counts it, as the figures file does. After the exploit, the wstETH a party paid or received in its own minting, redemptions and pool claims is shown with each of its actions.

## Compensation inputs

In wstETH, from the two readings around the exploit and the one at the pause; also in [BTC-stETH-compensation.json](BTC-stETH-compensation.json), in wei. A party's debt is its loss across the exploit's transaction. Where the capped rebalance paid its leveraged pool position more than it took, that gain is taken back from the party's leveraged reward where the reward is still unclaimed at the pause (the cut), and deducted from its debt where it is not.
